speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so let me actually follow this thread of the importance of goals and just being clear around this stuff.
zh: 好的，所以我实际上还是顺着这条线索，谈谈目标的重要性以及把事情搞清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have these six rules for creating clear goals and alignment on teams, talk about these six roles.
zh: 你有这六条规则来为团队创建明确的目标和一致性，谈谈这六个角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, totally.
zh: 是的，完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like there should be less than six but it's where we're at.
zh: 我觉得应该少于六条，但现状就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say, at a high level, two things before I get to the six.
zh: 我想说，在讲这六条之前，先从高层看两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is that I definitely have a bone to pick with OKRs, I feel like it's obviously been a really helpful framework for Google and others and, a lot of times, when I show up inside a company or I'm talking to a leader and I'm like, "What are your goals?"
zh: 第一，我确实对 OKRs 有意见，我觉得它显然对谷歌和其他人是一个非常有益的框架，而且很多时候，当我进入一家公司或者我在和一位领导者交谈时，我说：“你们的目标是什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: what I get back is this spreadsheet that has 100 lines and feels like it's written in Greek and, when I look at it, I'm like, " This doesn't create clarity for anyone."
zh: 我得到的回复是一个有 100 行的电子表格，感觉像是用希腊文写的，当我看着它时，我想：“这没有给任何人带来清晰感。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it brings me back to what is the point of goals, why do we have them and, at the end of the day, goals are a communication tool, that's what they are.
zh: 这让我回到了目标的重点，我们为什么要有目标，归根结底，目标是一种沟通工具，它们就是沟通工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're a communication tool designed to create clarity, to help people know I'm going to show up at my desk, what should I work on, what's the most important thing and your 100-line spreadsheet doesn't help anybody.
zh: 它们是一种旨在创造清晰度的沟通工具，帮助人们知道我要去工位上班了，我该做什么，最重要的事情是什么，而你的 100 行电子表格帮不了任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second thing I would just say is you really have to ask the question what is right for me at this company and this stage, what is right for a seed stage company is not what is right for a company that's got an established business and a clear go-to-market machine.
zh: 我要说的第二件事是，你真的必须问自己，在这个公司的这个阶段什么才是适合我的，适合种子阶段公司的不适合已经建立了成熟业务和明确推向市场机制的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, when I'm building in seed stage, I'm setting goals every two months in a very iterative way.
zh: 所以，当我在种子阶段建设时，我每两个月设定一次目标，以一种非常迭代的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I have an established business, I can actually set annual goals but annual goals for early stage companies is just a waste of time.
zh: 当我有了成熟的业务时，我实际上可以设定年度目标，但早期公司设定年度目标纯属浪费时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, anyway, a lot of my goal setting stuff actually comes from Facebook which I think was very, very good at this.
zh: 所以，不管怎样，我的很多目标设定的东西实际上来自 Facebook，我认为他们在这方面非常非常擅长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, the first role is that no company needs more than three company goals and the point of company goals is to help people know what the most important things are to success.
zh: 所以，第一条规则是，没有公司需要超过三个公司目标，公司目标的重点是帮助人们知道对成功来说最重要的事情是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, Facebook basically had three goals for the entire time I was there, it was five years and we did six-month goal setting, I think we did annual goal setting that ended up getting reset every six months but whatever.
zh: 所以，Facebook 基本上在我在那里的整个时间都有三个目标，那是五年，我们做六个月的目标设定，我想我们做了年度目标设定，结果每六个月就重置一次，但无所谓了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, the three goals were this, there was growth which was measured as monthly active users, that was the externally reported number eventually, MAUs.
zh: 所以，这三个目标是这样的，一个是增长，衡量指标是月活跃用户，那是最终对外报告的数字，MAUs。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second goal was engagement meaning how often do people come back and use the site and the third was revenue and we literally had three goals for the five years that I was there.
zh: 第二个目标是参与度，意思是人们多久回来一次并使用该网站，第三个是收入，在我那里的五年里，我们真的只有三个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you can govern that business with three goals, you can govern literally any business with three goals.
zh: 如果你能用三个目标管理那个业务，你就能用三个目标管理任何业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, no company needs more than three goals.
zh: 所以，没有公司需要超过三个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second thing is that one goal needs to win in a fight.
zh: 第二件事是，一个目标需要在冲突中胜出。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, if I'm sitting down and asking how do I prioritize my time on a given day I need to know what is the most important thing.
zh: 所以，如果我坐下来问我如何在特定的一天安排我的时间优先级，我需要知道最重要的事情是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Facebook, we had growth and there's a lot of different ways you can add monthly active users to a social media site including you can go buy a whole bunch of bots in Indonesia and that would add to your MAU number but it would not add to your engagement number and it was very clear for the entire time that I was there that engagement was the most important thing.
zh: 在 Facebook，我们有增长，有很多不同的方式可以为社交媒体网站增加月活跃用户，包括你可以去印度尼西亚买一大群机器人，这会增加你的 MAU 数字，但不会增加你的参与度数字，而且我在那里的整个时间里都很清楚，参与度是最重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Acquiring users that were going to use the site all the time, that's what drives revenue, it's also what drove the heart of that site.
zh: 获取那些会一直使用该网站的用户，这才是推动收入的动力，这也是驱动该网站核心的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, if you had to prioritize something, you prioritized engagement, that goal won in the fight.
zh: 所以，如果你必须优先考虑某件事，你就优先考虑参与度，那个目标在冲突中胜出了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third I'll say is, I call it the explain it to me like I'm five goal, but an intern that started on Monday should be able to look at your goals and understand them and, if they can't, then you are failing because they are not a communication tool that's effective.
zh: 第三点我想说的是，我称之为“像对我五岁那样解释”的目标，但一个周一入职的实习生应该能够看着你的目标并理解它们，如果他们不能，那你就失败了，因为它们不是一个有效的沟通工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to understand the goals, you have to explain the acronyms, you have to have numbers that make sense to average people, otherwise, again, it fails as a communication tool.
zh: 你必须能够理解这些目标，你必须解释这些缩写，你必须有对普通人有意义的数字，否则，再次强调，它作为沟通工具就失败了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fourth one is ... Actually, I stole a phrase from Claire Hughes Johnson who you've had on your podcast but wrote a book called Scaling People and in it she says this sentence that I love which is strategy should hurt.
zh: 第四个是……其实，我从 Claire Hughes Johnson 那里偷了一句话，你邀请过她上你的播客，但她写了一本书叫《Scaling People》，里面有一句话我很喜欢，说的是战略应该让人痛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my role used to be set non-goals, basically, make it as clear what you're not going to do as what you are going to do but strategy should hurt is a much better way to explain it to people which is, if you're not making trade-offs that are painful, you are not actually helping people prioritize their time.
zh: 我过去的角色是设定非目标，基本上，你要明确你不打算做什么，就像你明确你打算做什么一样，但“战略应该让人痛”是向人们解释这一点的一种更好的方式，也就是说，如果你没有做出痛苦的选择，你就没有真正帮助人们安排他们的时间优先级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the nature of work is that people will show up every day and do something and either you are very clear with them about what the priorities are or they're going to prioritize for you because they're going to choose what they work on every day.
zh: 因为工作的本质是人们每天都会出现并做某事，要么你对他们非常清楚优先事项是什么，要么他们会为你安排优先级，因为他们每天都会选择他们做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see this so much with founders where they can't cut things off the list, they just have to have the 10 goals and I'm like, "Cool.
zh: 我们在创始人身上经常看到这种情况，他们无法把事情从清单上划掉，他们必须有那 10 个目标，我就说：“酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Six of these goals are not going to get done so either you pick which four it is or other people are going to pick for you."
zh: 这六个目标不会完成，所以要么你挑出哪四个，要么其他人会替你挑。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So, strategy should hurt.
zh: 所以，战略应该让人痛。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your goal setting process is not painful, then you're not prioritizing heavily enough.
zh: 如果你的目标设定过程不痛苦，那么你的优先级排得还不够重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, ready?
zh: 好了吗，准备好了？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're on number five.
zh: 我们讲到第五条了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is more of an organizational point but it's really important for the waterline model too which is that one goal has one owner.
zh: 这更多是一个组织层面的观点，但对于水线模型也非常重要，那就是一个目标有一个负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a number, that number has a name next to it.
zh: 你有一个数字，那个数字旁边有一个名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you cannot do that work, you haven't done the most important work to actually make sure that these goals get accomplished.
zh: 如果你不能做这项工作，你就没有做确保这些目标完成的最重要的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's organizational work and it's very painful because sometimes it feels like, oh, this person can own it or this, maybe they'll just own it together, two people owning a goal is no one owning a goal.
zh: 而且这是组织工作，而且非常痛苦，因为有时感觉像，哦，这个人可以负责它，或者这个，也许他们只是一起负责它，两个人负责一个目标就是没有人负责目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: One person owns the goal, who is it?
zh: 一个人负责目标，是谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not you as the CEO, it's someone that works for you so one goal, one owner.
zh: 不是你作为 CEO，而是为你工作的人，所以一个目标，一个负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last, which is the hardest, is that goals by themselves are not enough.
zh: 最后一个，也是最难的，是光有目标是不够的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've spent a lot of time with founders that are like, "I did it.
zh: 我花了很多时间和那些说“我做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I set the goals.
zh: 我设定了目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not working?
zh: 为什么不起作用？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't understand."
zh: 我不明白。”的创始人在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, "What did you do after you set the goals?"
zh: 我就说：“你设定目标之后做了什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, "I don't know, I set the goals."
zh: 他们就说：“我不知道，我设定了目标。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Goals ...
zh: 目标……

speaker: Unknown
en: James Clear who wrote Atomic Habits has this really lovely sentence which is winners and losers have the same goal.
zh: 写了《原子习惯》的 James Clear 有句非常好的话，赢家和输家有着同样的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Goals by themself are not enough, you have to have a process by which you follow up on the goals and you hold people accountable to the goals and you learn from the goals because so much of goal setting, particularly if you're earlier in building your company, is about learning from trying to do something.
zh: 目标本身是不够的，你必须有一个流程来跟进目标，你要让大家对目标负责，你要从目标中学习，因为目标设定的很大一部分，特别是如果你在公司早期，就是从尝试做某事中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: You set a goal, can we do it, how hard is it to move this number, that is the ... You might be wrong all the time but you're learning what it takes to move the number.
zh: 你设定一个目标，我们能做到吗，推动这个数字有多难，这就是……你可能总是错的，但你学到了推动这个数字需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, setting the goal by itself, not enough, you have to build a process in the system to actually learn from the goal.
zh: 所以，仅设定目标是不够的，你必须在系统中建立一个流程，以真正从目标中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: This list is ... There's so much power in this list, it's such a succinct-
zh: 这个清单是……这个清单非常有力量，它是如此简洁——

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too long.
zh: 太长了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I don't think it is because each of these has so much depth and power to them that saves you so much headache and just wasted time and resources.
zh: 不，我不这么认为，因为这里的每一条都有如此深的内涵和力量，能为你省去那么多头疼的事，只是浪费的时间和资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just the idea of one owner, one goal, something I've personally discovered to have such power because, and correct me if I'm missing something here but just, if you feel like someone else may be doing the thing or feels like it's not just fully your responsibility, there's so much less energy and just mental ... I don't know.
zh: 仅仅是「一个负责人，一个目标」这个想法，我个人发现它非常有力量，因为，如果我漏掉了什么请纠正我，但只是，如果你觉得别人可能会在做这件事，或者觉得这不仅仅是你的全部责任，你的能量就会少得多，只是精神上……我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just don't care as much about hitting that goal.
zh: 你就是没有那么在乎达成那个目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's you-
zh: 如果是你——

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, accountability.
zh: 是的，问责制。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's like, "Lenny, this goal is your goal and, if you hit it, you've done it.
zh: 如果是这样，“Lenny，这个目标是你的目标，如果你达成了，你就做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't, you've done a bad job," that'd be a such motivating, so motivating.
zh: 如果你没达成，你就做得很糟糕，”这会非常激励人，太激励人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's me and Molly, okay, well, we'll figure it out.
zh: 如果是 Molly 和我，好吧，好吧，我们会解决的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It creates a flood of clarity that seeps down from the person too.
zh: 它创造了一股清晰的洪流，也会渗透到下面的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to go back to the waterline model, I would say, so often you'll actually find companies that have set goals but no one owns the goals, everyone owns the goals, multiple people own the goal and you didn't actually get all the way to the answer.
zh: 回到水线模型，我想说，很多时候你会真正发现那些设定了目标的公司，但没有人拥有目标，每个人都拥有目标，多个人拥有目标，而你没有真正找到最终的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I will say that the ownership thing is hard, it can feel painful but it's really important.
zh: 我想说的是，归属权这件事很难，可能会让人痛苦，但它真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's only one owner and that means that that person, come hell or high water, owns that number.
zh: 只有一个负责人，这意味着那个人，不管发生什么，都要为那个数字负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I described it [inaudible 00:55:18] was just someone's ass has to be on the line for this and that just works.
zh: 我描述它的方式 [听不清 00:55:18] 只是说必须有人的屁股为此担风险，这真的很管用。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's such a powerful lever to drive things to have one person responsible.
zh: 这是一个非常强大的杠杆，可以推动事情，让一个人负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other's just this idea of strategy hurting, I love that.
zh: 另一个只是「策略令人痛苦」这个想法，我喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that phrase, I forgot Claire had that.
zh: 我喜欢这个短语，我忘了 Claire 说过那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So true.
zh: 太真实了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So good.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the whole idea is you need to not do things, you need to decide what you're not ... The whole strategy, a big part of it is what we are not doing.
zh: 因为整个想法是你需要不做事，你需要决定你不在做……整个策略，很大一部分是我们不做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're not making painful choices, then you're not actually doing it.
zh: 如果你没有做出痛苦的选择，那么你就没有真正在做策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this idea of three goals, so is it just ... So, do you go into a company and just go through a checklist essentially of here's the six things I look at to tell me where there's opportunity to improve?
zh: 还有「三个目标」这个想法，那么它只是……那么，你进入一家公司，只是走过一个清单，本质上这是我关注的六件事，来告诉我哪里有机会改进？

speaker: Unknown
en: When I work with founders and I see their goals, I use it as a way to get to know the business and I'm just going to be literally like, "What is this?
zh: 当我与创始人合作，看到他们的目标时，我把它作为一种了解业务的方式，我就只是字面上像，“这是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you trying to explain?"
zh: 你想解释什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can usually, through asking a lot of really dumb questions which, like I said, one of my superpowers, get them to explain to me the one sentence and the one number that they're actually trying to get across but it takes work and that's part of ... It's almost easier to write the 100-line spreadsheet than it is to say, "Wait, what are the three drivers of this business genuinely?
zh: 我通常可以通过问很多真的很傻的问题，这就像我说的，我的超能力之一，让他们向我解释他们真正想要传达的那一句话和那一个数字，但这需要努力，这也是……写一个 100 行的电子表格可能比说“等等，这个业务的真正驱动力是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are they and how do they relate to each other?"
zh: 它们是什么，它们如何相互关联？”要容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there can be things underneath them but there's three at the top that matter.
zh: 下面可以有东西，但顶层有三个是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, I'm not a scientific person about it but a lot of it is just by asking people to explain their businesses to me, you can basically find the drivers.
zh: 所以，是的，我在这方面不是一个科学的人，但很多时候只是通过让人们向我解释他们的业务，你基本上就能找到驱动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the story about Facebook having these same three goals for five years, considering their success, you may think they're not as complicated as your business but I am confident they're just as, if not, more complicated.
zh: 关于 Facebook 五年来都有这三个同样的目标的故事，考虑到他们的成功，你可能认为他们不如你的业务复杂，但我确信他们只是，如果不是，更复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're a marketplace, a social network, they're a ad business, just they're ... There's a lot going on and, if they can work with three goals, you can do that too.
zh: 他们是一个市场，一个社交网络，他们是一个广告业务，只是他们……有很多事情在进行，如果他们能用三个目标工作，你也可以做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to your point, if it's not hurting, then you're doing something wrong.
zh: 说到你的观点，如果它不让人痛苦，那么你就做错了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love how ... This is very much what I wanted this chat to be.
zh: 我喜欢……这正是我希望这次聊天成为的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like every little segment is its own, could be its own podcast where we could talk about this for hours so I'm really excited how this is going.
zh: 感觉每一个小片段都是它自己的，可以是它自己的播客，我们可以谈论这个好几个小时，所以我真的很兴奋这进行得如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: Moving on to another topic, you have not necessarily rules but rules of thumb that you find really helpful for people to have in their head as they're dealing with change and scale and growth and all that kind of stuff so let's just walk through that.
zh: 转到另一个话题，你不一定有规则，但有经验法则，你发现这对人们非常有帮助，让他们在脑海中记住，当他们处理变化、规模、增长和所有这类事情时，所以让我们过一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for leaders that are leading through change and growth, the list is probably long but I always say to people don't come to me for management 101, I'm not the person to ask on how to run the most effective one-on-one with your people.
zh: 所以，对于通过变化和增长来领导的领导者来说，这个清单可能很长，但我总是对人们说不要来找我寻求管理 101，我不是那个关于如何与你的下属进行最有效的一对一的问题的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I think is not talked about enough is what it takes to manage and lead through change and that is a very particular set of feelings.
zh: 我认为人们谈论得不够的是通过变化来管理和领导需要什么，这是一组非常特殊的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first thing I learned, when someone makes you a manager or when you take a job as a leader inside a company, you really do feel like, "Oh, who gave me this job?"
zh: 我学到的第一件事，当有人让你成为经理，或者当你在公司内部担任领导工作时，你真的感觉像，“哦，谁给了我这份工作？”

speaker: Unknown
en: and you feel like you're supposed to know the answer to things.
zh: 你觉得你应该知道事情的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: People come to you and ask questions and you're like, "I'm supposed to know.
zh: 人们来找你问问题，你会想，“我应该知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a leader, I am supposed to have answers."
zh: 我是领导者，我应该有答案。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, particularly inside of rapid change and scale and growth, it's really important to understand that your job as manager and a leader is not to have all the answers.
zh: 我认为，特别是在快速变化、规模扩大和增长的背景下，理解作为管理者和领导者的工作不是拥有所有答案，这一点非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is not to have all the answers, it is to get good at finding them, it is to get good at bringing people together to find the answers.
zh: 不是要拥有所有答案，而是要擅长找到答案，是擅长把人们聚集在一起找到答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is hard because it requires saying, "I don't know, let's go figure it out," a whole bunch and it's scary as a leader to say I don't know because you think, "Oh, gosh, people are going to see through me."
zh: 这很难，因为这需要不断地说，“我不知道，让我们去弄清楚，”作为领导者说这很可怕，因为你会想，“天哪，人们会看穿我。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, the more you travel in life, the more you realize that the most experienced leaders are the ones that say, "No, no, no," all the time.
zh: 但同样，你在生活中走得越远，你就越意识到最有经验的领导者是那些总是说“不，不，不”的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is a good reminder of this Bob the monster concept because, hearing this, okay, I don't need to have all the answers as a leader.
zh: 我认为这是对怪物 Bob 这个概念的一个很好的提醒，因为听到这个，好吧，作为领导者我不需要拥有所有答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: In real life, being in a meeting, people are like, "Hey, Molly, what do you think of this?"
zh: 在现实生活中，在一个会议上，人们会说，“嘿，Molly，你觉得这个怎么样？”

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, "Oh, I should have a good answer."
zh: 你会想，“噢，我应该有一个好的答案。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I think that's a good reminder of this idea of this Bob the monster is going to tell you, "Oh, you don't know anything, you're not ready for this.
zh: 所以，我认为这是对怪物 Bob 这个想法的一个很好的提醒，怪物 Bob 会告诉你，“噢，你什么都不知道，你还没准备好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You suck at this, you're going to fail everyone that's [inaudible 00:59:34]."
zh: 你对此很烂，你会让所有人失望，那是 [听不清 00:59:34]。”

speaker: Unknown
en: They're regretting hiring you.
zh: 他们后悔雇佣了你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，正是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's going to see through you.
zh: 每个人都会看穿你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imposter, imposter, imposter.
zh: 冒名顶替者，冒名顶替者，冒名顶替者。

speaker: Lenny
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Molly Graham
en: Yeah, 100%.
zh: 是的，百分之百。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just remembering, there's going to be this part of your head and that's okay, it's there but it doesn't mean it's true.
zh: 但只要记住，你的脑海中会有这一部分，这没关系，它在那里但这并不意味着它是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these things are muscles.
zh: 这些东西都是肌肉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dealing with Bob as a muscle, learning to not react to all those things that attack you but also learning, oh, in this moment when someone asks me a question and I'm like, "Oh," actually I should be like, "I don't actually know, let's go ... Who should we ask?
zh: 应对 Bob 是一种肌肉，学会不对所有攻击你的事情做出反应，还要学会，噢，在这个时刻，当有人问我一个问题而我想，“噢”，实际上我应该像，“我真的不知道，让我们去……我们应该问谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we learn this?
zh: 我们该如何学习这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we explore this together?
zh: 我们该如何一起探索这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think?"
zh: 你怎么认为？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are all actually very powerful questions and they're terrifying to, particularly earlier in your career, as a leader and a manager.
zh: 这些实际上都是非常有力的问题，而且在你的职业生涯早期，作为领导者和管理者，这些问题是可怕的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah, so the lesson there is no one expects you to have all the answers as a leader.
zh: 所以，是的，那里的教训是，没有人期望你作为领导者拥有所有答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And particularly in this world, the one that's changing as fast as it is, nobody knows.
zh: 特别是在这个世界里，变化如此之快，没有人知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody knows what the answers are in a lot of cases, the war will be won by the people that are good exploring and figuring it out.
zh: 在许多情况下没有人知道答案是什么，胜利将属于那些擅长探索和弄清楚的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that phrase.
zh: 我喜欢这个短语。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, the second one is, and everyone that has learned this has learned it the hard way, do not promise things that you can't control.
zh: 所以，第二点是，每个学过这一点的人都学得很艰难，不要承诺你无法控制的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so tempting particularly when you're hiring people to be like, "Oh, yeah, your onboarding will be smooth and calm and everything's clear and we've figured it ... Let us tell you our vision and how obvious and clear and smart and blah, blah, blah."
zh: 这特别诱人，尤其是当你雇佣人时，会说，“噢，是的，你的入职会很顺利平静，一切都清楚，我们已经搞定了……让我们告诉你我们的愿景，它是多么明显和聪明，等等等等。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they show up and it's like, "Oh, shit," you know what I mean?
zh: 然后他们来了，就像是，“噢，该死，”你懂我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no manual, no one knows what they're doing, it's all ambiguity and chaos.
zh: 没有手册，没有人知道他们在做什么，一切都是模棱两可和混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so easy when someone says I want to know that I'm going to be your CMO forever to be like, "Sure, you can be my CMO," you don't know that.
zh: 当有人说我想知道我会永远成为你的 CMO 时，很容易说，“当然，你可以做我的 CMO，”你并不知道那。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, being really careful with promises of things that are out of your control like stability or titles or never hiring over someone is a flashing red light because there is literally no faster way to demoralize high performers than going back on a promise.
zh: 所以，对那些超出你控制范围的事情的承诺要非常小心，比如稳定性、头衔或者绝不在某人之上雇佣人，这是一个闪烁的红灯，因为实际上没有比违背承诺更快的方式来打击高绩效者了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone that has been through it knows that feeling of like, "They told me this when I joined," and then they don't do it and you're like, "Well, fuck this place."
zh: 每个经历过这种事的人都有这种感觉，“他们加入时告诉了我这个，”然后他们没有做到，你会想，“好吧，去他妈的这地方。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So, no faster way to demoralize people or to hire the wrong people than promising things that are actually out of your control.
zh: 所以，没有比承诺那些实际上超出你控制范围的事情更快的方式来打击士气或雇佣错误的人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Being honest and upfront about who you are as a company, about what you're able to promise, all of that is actually ... It's very hard work but it's so important because so much is out of your control and you need to hire people that are cool with that.
zh: 诚实地坦率地作为公司你是谁，关于你能承诺什么，所有这些实际上……这是非常艰苦的工作，但它非常重要，因为太多事情超出了你的控制，你需要雇佣那些对此很酷的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love that.
zh: 喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned this the hard way once, I had a ... One of my early projects, we were late and the head of product was just so pissed he's like, "Because I've been telling the CEO it's going to be on time because you've been telling me it's going to be on time and then it wasn't and why didn't you tell me that?"
zh: 我有一次艰难地学会了这一点，我有一个……我的早期项目之一，我们迟到了，产品负责人非常生气，他说，“因为我一直在告诉 CEO 它会准时，因为你一直在告诉我它会准时，然后它没有，你为什么不告诉我那个？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was just like, "Okay, it'll never happen again," and he's like, "You can't ... Don't tell me that because that's not true, that nay not ... You can't guarantee that."
zh: 我只是说，“好的，这再也不会发生了，”他说，“你不能……别告诉我那个，因为那不是真的，那不可……你不能保证那个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, that taught me that lesson of just, yeah, you're right, you want to say that, it feels so good.
zh: 所以，那教会了我这一课，是的，你是对的，你想说那个，感觉很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, this will never happen again but you can't and they know you can't promise things like that.
zh: 好的，这再也不会发生了，但你不能，而且他们知道你不能承诺那样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sorry, I'm going to quote Claire Hughes Johnson again but she has this really fun phrase that she said in a talk at Glue Club that I've now latched onto and stolen from her which is, she was like, "Promises like that are like letter bombs that you mail yourself that are going to explode in your face in a year," and I was like, "That is the perfect metaphor."
zh: 抱歉，我要再次引用 Claire Hughes Johnson，但她在 Glue Club 的演讲中有一个非常有趣的短语，我现在已经采纳并从她那里偷过来了，她说，“那样的承诺就像你寄给自己的信件炸弹，会在一年后在你的脸上爆炸，”我想，“那是完美的隐喻。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's short-term pain, you want to make this person feel good right now so you promise them something but, in one year, you're going to make them feel terrible so don't do it.
zh: 因为这是短期痛苦，你想让这个人现在感觉良好，所以你向他们承诺了某事，但在一年后，你会让他们感觉很糟糕，所以别这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great advice.
zh: 很好的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, keep going.
zh: 好的，继续。

speaker: Molly Graham
en: Yeah. So, again, could probably go on the topic of what it takes to manage and lead forever inside this stuff but I'll give you two more that I yell about a lot in Glue Club. The first is that we spend huge amounts of time talking about hiring. How do you get good at hiring? What's the right interview? How do I find the right people? Firing people is as important as hiring people. Getting good at identifying when someone does not belong or someone is not going to work out is actually a skill and being good at it as a company and as a leader is as important as identifying the right talent because, eventually, if you're not good at firing people, what you have is essentially barnacles on a ship. Really going forward with the ship metaphor, anyway.
zh: 是的。所以，同样，关于管理和领导在这个领域需要什么，这个话题可能可以永远聊下去，但我会再给你两个我在 Glue Club 经常大声疾呼的观点。首先是我们花了大量时间讨论招聘。如何擅长招聘？什么是正确的面试？我如何找到合适的人？解雇员工和招聘员工一样重要。擅长识别某人何时不属于这里或某人何时行不通实际上是一项技能，作为公司和领导者擅长此道与识别合适的人才一样重要，因为最终，如果你不擅长解雇员工，你拥有的本质上是船上的藤壶。真的延续船的隐喻，反正就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's true.
zh: 是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's drag people that are sitting around not pushing the team forward.
zh: 这是一种阻力，那些坐在周围不推动团队前进的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it's painful and it's horrible because it is humans but, when someone doesn't fit, you ... No one is right all the time when it comes to hiring, I actually say most people are wrong half the time.
zh: 所以，这是痛苦的和可怕的，因为这是人类，但是，当某人不适合时，你……在招聘方面没有人是一直正确的，我实际上说大多数人在一半的时间里都是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best people in the world in hiring will tell you they have about a 50% average in terms of being right.
zh: 世界上在招聘方面最优秀的人会告诉你，他们在正确性方面大约有 50% 的平均成功率。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means half the hires don't work out.
zh: 这意味着一半的招聘没有成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means, half the time, you're going to need to fire the person.
zh: 这意味着，在一半的时间里，你需要解雇这个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, it's such an important skill to get good at particularly when you're going through a lot of change.
zh: 所以，这是一项非常重要的需要擅长的技能，特别是当你经历大量变化时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the last one is humans are messy and it's very emotional.
zh: 最后一点是，人类是混乱的，而且非常有情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you're a leader, particularly if you have any kind of anagram too or just if you like to make people happy and you want to be liked, it can be so hard to lead teams because you get tangled in the people.
zh: 当你是一名领导者，特别是如果你有任何字谜游戏或者只是如果你喜欢让人们快乐并且你想被喜欢，领导团队可能会非常困难，因为你卷入了人际关系中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Firing people is a painful experience, reorganizing things, layering people, all these things are emotionally painful for the people and they're emotionally painful for you as a manager.
zh: 解雇员工是一种痛苦的经历，重组事情，人员分层，所有这些事情对人们在情感上是痛苦的，对你作为管理者在情感上也是痛苦的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But my mantra that almost always leads in the best direction is serve the business, not the people meaning everyone is better off if this company is wildly successful.
zh: 但我的几乎总是指向最佳方向的座右铭是服务于业务，而不是服务于人，意味着如果这家公司疯狂地成功，每个人都会过得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone looks smart and makes lots of money or whatever if this company grows and does what we all dream it can.
zh: 如果这家公司发展并实现我们梦想它能做到的事情，每个人看起来都很聪明并赚很多钱或其他什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, at the end of the day, the best decisions, the ones that are always going to be right are the ones that are like, "How do we do the right thing for this business?"
zh: 所以，归根结底，最好的决定，那些总是正确的决定，就是那些像“我们如何为这家业务做正确的事情？”的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it also helps in political situations.
zh: 这在政治局势中也有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone's acting weird or their Bob is raging all over the company, technically, everyone has the same goal.
zh: 某人表现得很奇怪，或者他们的 Bob 在整个公司里 raging，从技术上讲，每个人都有相同的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal is to build the biggest business possible, that's the answer.
zh: 目标是建立尽可能大的业务，这就是答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer is always what's the right thing for the business.
zh: 答案总是对业务来说什么是正确的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the people stuff can fall away when you actually focus on what's the right thing for the business.
zh: 当你实际上专注于对业务来说什么是正确的事情时，人员的事情可能会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: A really useful tool to do that that I learned from my manager is to think about, when you're trying to decide whether to fire someone or change a project even though it's going to upset someone, is to say, "Okay, if there were no emotions involved, if this person had no negative reaction to this, what would I do?"
zh: 一个真正有用的工具，这是我从我的经理那里学到的，就是思考，当你试图决定是否解雇某人或改变一个项目即使这会让某人不安时，要说，“好吧，如果不涉及情绪，如果这个人对这个没有负面反应，我会做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全。

speaker: Lenny
en: And then that's the thing you should do and then you just do it. And then the question is how do I communicate this to them where their pain is lowest essentially.
zh: 那么那就是你应该做的事情，然后你就去做。然后问题是我如何向他们传达这一点，使他们的痛苦基本上是最低的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the kindest way possible.
zh: 以尽可能善良的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the kindest way possible.
zh: 以尽可能善良的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because, to your point, if you optimize for the other thing of making people feel good, everything just falls apart, they're going to suffer even more down the road.
zh: 因为，正如你所指出的，如果你为了另一件事——让人们感觉良好——而进行优化，一切都会崩溃，他们以后会遭受更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Direct is kind.
zh: 直接就是善良。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels kind or, really, honestly, easy to avoid these things or to work around them or to not but, at the end of the day, it's basically just a drag, the barnacle thing.
zh: 这感觉像是善良，或者真的，老实说，很容易回避这些事情，或者绕过它们，或者不这样做，但归根结底，这基本上只是一种阻力，藤壶这种事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It drags on your company, on your time, on your energy, et cetera.
zh: 它拖累你的公司，你的时间，你的精力等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, very hard to do in real life to do the thing that's hard and cause someone to be sad and upset and frustrated and maybe leave.
zh: 但同样，在现实生活中很难做到这一点，去做这件困难的事情，并导致某人悲伤、不安和沮丧，甚至可能离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is so hard and all these things are muscles, you get better at ... They don't become easy, it's not like anybody who's like, "Oh, it's so ... I enjoy firing people," no, but you recognize it faster and you are like, "Oh, I need to go do this."
zh: 这是如此困难，所有这些事情都是肌肉，你会变得更好……它们不会变得容易，并不像任何人会说，“噢，这太……我喜欢解雇人，”不，但你识别它的速度更快了，你会像，“噢，我需要去做这件事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is actually ... It's a practice and something that you need to practice to become the kind of leader that leads these long-enduring companies.
zh: 这实际上……这是一种实践，也是你需要练习的东西，以便成为那种领导这些长久公司的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this tool of thinking, asking what would I do if there were no emotions involved and this person wouldn't be upset, it helps you realize, okay, I see, this actually doesn't make sense to just do it the easy way right now because it doesn't make sense.
zh: 还有这种思考工具，问如果不涉及情绪以及这个人不会不安我会做什么，它帮助你意识到，好吧，我明白了，现在以简单的方式去做实际上是没有意义的，因为没有意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it strips away.
zh: 是的，它剥离了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It strips away the emotions.
zh: 它剥离了情绪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something else I wanted to make sure we spent a little time on is you have another tidbit along these lines which is around putting most of your energy into high performers versus spending all your time people that need help, talk about that.
zh: 还有一件事我想确保我们花点时间讨论的是，你有一个与此相关的小贴士，关于将大部分精力投入高绩效员工而不是花费所有时间在需要帮助的人身上，谈谈那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a leader, as a manager, you're running these teams and someone's struggling and it's very easy to get dragged into that and to end up spending a huge amount of energy on it but high performers are actually the future of your company.
zh: 作为领导者，作为管理者，你管理这些团队，某人在挣扎，很容易被拖进去并最终花费大量精力在这上面，但高绩效员工实际上是你公司的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about it and if you've spent time on it, those are the folks where, if you invest your time and energy in them, you're going to get the 10x return that people talk about all the time in Silicon Valley.
zh: 如果你考虑一下，如果你花时间在上面，这些人就是，如果你投入时间和精力在他们身上，你会得到人们一直在硅谷谈论的 10 倍回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I've witnessed is that most people have a high performer and they just leave them alone, they're like, "That person's doing well so I'm just going to let them do their thing."
zh: 但我目睹的是，大多数人有一个高绩效员工，他们只是不理会他们，他们就像，“那个人做得很好，所以我就让他们做他们的事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I do when I have a high performer that's my favorite thing in the world is invest time and energy in them and basically build a whole system of working with them that is designed to draw out potential.
zh: 而当我有一个高绩效员工时，那是我在世界上最喜欢的事情，就是投入时间和精力在他们身上，基本上建立一个与他们合作的整个系统，旨在挖掘潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say there's two things here, one is it's really important to realize that our tendency-
zh: 我想这里有两件事，一件是很重要的一点，我们的倾向是——

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two things here.
zh: 这里有两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is it's really important to realize that our tendency is to actually spend time on low performers and it is not a good use of your time.
zh: 一件是很重要的一点，意识到我们的倾向实际上是花时间在低绩效员工身上，这不是对你时间的好利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: See the point about firing people.
zh: 参见关于解雇人的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the other thing is that actively investing in and developing high performers is something that's important to get good at as a leader because that is how you create these little rocket ships that end up... You'll manage someone who's just like a project manager and all of a sudden they're running a whole function inside the company eventually, but it's because you took time and energy to invest in them.
zh: 但另一件事是，积极投资和发展高绩效员工是作为领导者需要擅长的事情，因为这就是你创造这些最终会……小火箭的方法，你会管理一个只是项目经理的人，突然有一天他们在公司内部负责整个职能，但这是因为你投入了时间和精力在他们身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my basic way of doing that, not to... I could spend a long time on this, but I would just say is I run experiments.
zh: 我做这件事的基本方式，不是去……我可以在这上面花很长时间，但我只想说我做实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I basically develop a theory about someone, "I think this person is capable of this kind of thing."
zh: 我基本上就是针对某人提出一个理论，“我觉得这个人有能力做这种事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then piece by piece, it doesn't have to be a whole job or whole project.
zh: 然后一点一点来，这不必是整个工作或整个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can just be an incremental experiment, "I'm going to see if they can do this with less guidance or support from me."
zh: 它可能只是一个增量实验，“我要看看他们能不能在我不怎么指导或支持的情况下做这件事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to give them a bigger project.
zh: 我要给他们一个更大的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to give them something with more visibility.
zh: 我要给他们更有曝光度的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to manage them less, oversee them less, whatever.
zh: 我要少管理他们，少监督他们，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of those are experiments to basically test your theory and deepen your theory in terms of this person's potential and their ability to help the company.
zh: 所有这些实验都是为了基本上验证你的理论，并加深你对这个人的潜力和他们帮助公司的能力的理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're basically, for me, what I'm doing is deeply getting to know that person and then trying to pair them with company needs.
zh: 而基本上，对我来说，我正在做的是深入了解那个人，然后试图将他们与公司的需求配对。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we need?
zh: 我们需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This person is great at zebra farming.
zh: 这个人在斑马养殖方面很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do we need zebra farming?
zh: 我们哪里需要斑马养殖？

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do I get them working on bigger and bigger and more and more critical things?
zh: 那么我如何让他们去做越来越重要、越来越关键的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be honest, this is what people have done for me.
zh: 老实说，这也是人们对我做过的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: At Facebook in particular, I've benefited from people being like, "Ooh, come help me with this thing."
zh: 特别是在 Facebook，我受益于人们说，“噢，来帮我做这件事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: They saw potential in me and they asked me to help with something and it unlocked a huge amount for me.
zh: 他们在我身上看到了潜力，他们让我帮忙做某事，这为我解锁了巨大的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, it is such a powerful tool for getting more out of people that might be a little bit stuck if you leave them in this box.
zh: 因此，这是一个非常强大的工具，如果你把这些人留在框框里，他们可能有点受困。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you start to expand the box, you can really unlock people.
zh: 但如果你开始扩大这个框框，你真的可以解锁人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So speaking of high performers, you've worked with many very high performing founder-CEOs.
zh: 说到高绩效人士，你与许多非常高绩效的创始人兼 CEO 合作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: He worked really closely with Zuck, with Cheryl Sandberg, with Larry and Sergei at Google, with Brett Taylor, who I just... Just like you trying to read his resume, it takes three lines of things he's done over the course of his career.
zh: 他与 Zuck、Cheryl Sandberg、Google 的 Larry 和 Sergei，以及 Brett Taylor 密切合作过，我刚刚……就像你试图读他的简历一样，他职业生涯中做过的事情需要三行字才能写完。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I just want to spend a little time on what are some things you've learned, maybe a few things you've learned from them, that group that you find yourself sharing with other people most.
zh: 所以我只想花点时间谈谈你学到的一些东西，也许是你从他们身上学到的几样东西，也就是你发现自己最常与其他人分享的那个群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: That list is very long, but I'll give you a couple.
zh: 那个名单很长，但我给你讲几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one that I think is kind of counterintuitive is... So I said I worked at Facebook.
zh: 我认为第一个有点反直觉的是……所以我说我在 Facebook 工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked on culture, which is one of those words that doesn't really mean anything.
zh: 我从事文化工作，这是那些并不真正意味着什么的词之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I define it as the way we do things around here.
zh: 所以我将其定义为我们在这里做事的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought my job was to shape the culture.
zh: 我以为我的工作是塑造文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought it was to push the culture.
zh: 我以为它是推动文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the most humbling lesson I learned is 80% of the culture of a company is literally defined by the personality of the founder.
zh: 我学到的最令人谦卑的教训是，一家公司 80% 的文化实际上是由创始人的个性定义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook is Mark.
zh: Facebook 就是 Mark。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google is Larry and Sergei.
zh: Google 就是 Larry 和 Sergei。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google, when I was there, it felt like a university.
zh: 当我在那里时，Google 感觉像一所大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's where ideas are more important in a lot of ways than what's shipped.
zh: 在很多方面，想法比交付的东西更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a campus and they basically wanted people to live there when I was there.
zh: 有一个校园，当我还在那里时，他们基本上希望人们住在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was designed to basically be a two PhD students' paradise.
zh: 它的设计基本上是两个博士生的天堂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook felt like a 19-year-old hacker's dorm room when I was there.
zh: 当我在那里时，Facebook 感觉像一个 19 岁的黑客宿舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was shipping above all and all else.
zh: 它是交付至上，其他一切都不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seeped with Mark's DNA.
zh: 它渗透着 Mark 的 DNA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I spent ages trying to create various changes inside the company or trying to push a point.
zh: 我花了很长时间试图在公司内部创造各种变化或试图推动某一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Mark would say literally one thing in an all hands, and it was like somebody threw a boulder into the pond.
zh: 而 Mark 会在全体会议上只说一件事，这就像有人往池塘里扔了一块巨石。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our job as operators or as leaders around founders is to help articulate the culture that they're creating and to help extend it.
zh: 所以我们作为运营者或创始人周围领导者的工作是，帮助阐明他们正在创造的文化，并帮助扩展它。

speaker: Unknown
en: My version of founder mode, which I know you've spent some time on on this podcast is your job is to build a company that would make a decision the way the founder would when they're not in the room.
zh: 我对创始人模式的理解，我知道你在这个播客上花了一些时间，就是你的工作是建立一家这样的公司：当创始人不在房间里时，它会像创始人那样做决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the work of building a company around a founder, but your job is not to shape culture.
zh: 这是围绕创始人建立一家公司的工作，但你的工作不是塑造文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is mostly defined by the literal personality strengths and weaknesses of the person at the top.
zh: 这在很大程度上是由处于顶层的人的实际个性和优缺点定义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's been true of Mark and it's been true of Brett.
zh: 这对于 Mark 来说是真的，对于 Brett 来说也是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everywhere I go, that's who it is.
zh: 无论我去哪里，都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need a consulting firm to tell you, just go do a personality diagnosis on your founder.
zh: 你不需要咨询公司来告诉你，只要去对你的创始人做一个性格诊断。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the weaknesses thing is real.
zh: 而且缺点这一点是真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen and watched friends try to shape a set of values at a company and it just doesn't match who the founder is.
zh: 我见过并看着朋友们试图在公司中塑造一套价值观，但这与创始人的身份不符。

speaker: Unknown
en: You say, "Move fast and break things," or whatever your version of that is.
zh: 你说，“快速行动，打破常规”，或者你的任何版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your founder loves ambiguity and is perfectly happy with not making decisions.
zh: 而你的创始人喜欢模糊不清，并且非常乐意不做决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: All that leads to is cultural dissonance.
zh: 所有这一切导致的只是文化上的不协调。

speaker: Unknown
en: It leads to people being like, "Wait, what?
zh: 它会导致人们说，“等等，什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought we said we care about moving fast and making aggressive decisions and it turns out..." So being really careful about what you say, because what people actually feel when it comes to culture is what you do and how you act every day.
zh: 我以为我们说过我们关心快速行动和做出激进的决定，结果却是……”所以要非常注意你所说的话，因为人们在文化中实际感受到的是你每天的行为和举止。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can never write anything down and you will still have a culture.
zh: 你永远不需要写下任何东西，你仍然会有一种文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be created through the actions and the decisions that you make and that your founder makes.
zh: 它将通过你和你创始人所采取的行动和所做的决定而创造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that would be a huge one.
zh: 所以这将是一件非常重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me spend a little more time on this because this is so good.
zh: 让我在这个问题上多花点时间，因为这太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all this advice on culture and it feels so true based on everything I've seen.
zh: 所以所有这些关于文化的建议，根据我所看到的一切，感觉如此真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So tip one there is just you can't really change the culture.
zh: 所以那里的第一点建议就是你无法真正改变文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there's a little bit on the edges you could adjust.
zh: 也许在边缘有一些地方你可以调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will come down and trickle down from the founder, CEO probably mostly, but just the founders in general.
zh: 它将自上而下地从创始人那里渗透下来，CEO 可能是主要的，但通常就是指创始人。

speaker: Molly Graham
en: And founder-CEO is probably the single biggest.
zh: 而创始人-CEO 可能是唯一最重要的因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founder-CEO.
zh: 创始人-CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Co-founders, it depends a lot on the company.
zh: 联合创始人，这在很大程度上取决于公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Stripe is probably very much like Patrick and John, but it's not every co-founder that has that level of power [inaudible 01:15:03].
zh: 我想 Stripe 非常像 Patrick 和 John，但并不是每个联合创始人都有那种级别的权力 [听不清 01:15:03]。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the way you describe culture, I think it's the way Seth Godin talks about it too, who's also been on the podcast.
zh: 然后你描述文化的方式，我认为这也是 Seth Godin 谈论它的方式，他也上过这个播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: How cool is that?
zh: 那多酷啊？

speaker: Unknown
en: So cool.
zh: 太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, "Culture is..." And what you said, "Culture is the way we do things around here.
zh: 他说，“文化是……”而你说过，“文化就是我们在这里的做事方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what culture is, is how we..." That's how people describe your culture is, "The way we do things around here."
zh: 这就是文化，就是我们要……”这就是人们描述你的文化的方式，“我们在这里的做事方式。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I ran culture, whatever the hell that means, at Facebook for a hot second.
zh: 我在 Facebook 管过文化，不管那到底意味着什么，有那么一瞬间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I literally haven't done a values exercise since.
zh: 从那以后我真的再也没有做过价值观练习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it sounds crazy, right?
zh: 听起来很疯狂，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because in theory, I know how to do this stuff.
zh: 因为理论上，我知道怎么做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't really know how to do this stuff.
zh: 我其实并不知道怎么做这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for me, the point is process and systems and how do we make decisions?
zh: 但对我来说，重点是流程和系统以及我们要如何做决定？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where culture actually lives.
zh: 那才是文化真正存在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is what you do.
zh: 那就是你所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how you hire.
zh: 那是你如何招聘的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's how you fire.
zh: 那是你如何解雇的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's who you don't hire.
zh: 那是你不招聘谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all of those decisions.
zh: 那是所有那些决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is culture.
zh: 那就是文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whenever I'm working with a company or building a company, that's what I'm focused on, not on what's the shiny word that we're putting on the wall.
zh: 所以每当我和一家公司合作或建立一家公司时，那就是我关注的重点，而不是我们要把什么闪亮的词汇挂在墙上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the way you're describing is, as you said, it's what you do.
zh: 所以你描述的方式是，正如你所说，它是你所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not what you say?
zh: 而不是你所说的？

en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

en: Keep going.
zh: 继续。

en: I'll give you two more that are helpful.
zh: 我会再给你两个有帮助的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one is a Mark Zuckerberg classic, but he has this very strong feeling that people don't escalate enough.
zh: 这是一个 Mark Zuckerberg 的经典观点，但他有一种非常强烈的感觉，就是人们升级得不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was very adamant about it at Facebook.
zh: 他在 Facebook 对此非常坚定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he brought it to CZI too where he was like, "Escalation is a tool."
zh: 他也把它带到了 CZI，他在那里说，“升级是一种工具。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, "People get stuck.
zh: 他说，“人们会被困住。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get stuck with two people with equal power trying to solve a problem.
zh: 当两个权力相当的人试图解决一个问题时，他们会陷入僵局。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can spend so much time bashing heads, going back and forth.
zh: 你可以花很多时间去互相碰撞，来来回回。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually what you just need to do is go up.
zh: 实际上你需要做的就是向上走。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to go."
zh: 你需要去。"

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem is that we think of escalation as, "I'm A and B and I are disagreeing.
zh: 问题在于我们将升级视为，“我是 A，B 和我有分歧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I'm going to go up to C and tell on B. I'm going to go tattle to the teacher."
zh: 所以我要去找 C 并告发 B。我要去向老师打小报告。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not what escalation is.
zh: 这不是升级。

speaker: Unknown
en: What escalation is, "We disagree.
zh: 升级是，“我们有分歧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Neither one of us has enough power to make this decision.
zh: 我们俩都没有足够的权力来做这个决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go to someone who does."
zh: 让我们去找一个有权力的人。”

speaker: Unknown
en: My boss, my boss's boss, whoever it is.
zh: 我的老板，我老板的老板，无论谁都可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as you are stuck, escalate.
zh: 一旦你陷入僵局，就升级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go together, go make your case to whoever it is, go together up.
zh: 一起去，去向相关负责人陈述你们的理由，一起向上走。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is unlocking.
zh: 这就是解锁。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's saving you a whole bunch of time.
zh: 这能为你节省大量时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's something that I've found as I've worked with companies and leaders in Glue Club.
zh: 这是我在与公司合作以及在 Glue Club 与领导者共事时发现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not a muscle that's very comfortable for people, but it's so smart.
zh: 这不是一种人们感到舒适的肌肉，但它非常明智。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Mark has a lot of these, but that one I really took away because again, I think so many people think of escalation as bad, a failure, like, "I failed, so I had to escalate."
zh: Mark 有很多这样的做法，但我真正记住了这一条，因为同样，我认为很多人认为升级是坏事，是失败，比如，“我失败了，所以我不得不升级。”

speaker: Unknown
en: No, it's a tool.
zh: 不，它是一个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what management is for.
zh: 这就是管理存在的意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're there to unblock you.
zh: 他们就是为了解除你的阻塞而存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let them unblock you.
zh: 让他们为你解除阻塞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stop arguing over something you can't decide.
zh: 停止争论你们无法决定的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they'll be so happy knowing you did not waste a week debating this and then just arguing and just looking at data.
zh: 他们会很高兴，知道你没有浪费一周时间来辩论这个，然后只是争吵和只是看数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, "Okay, I can just tell you exactly what we should do.
zh: 这就像，“好的，我可以直接告诉你们我们应该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go do that."
zh: 让我们去做吧。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You lack context or you lack power.
zh: 你缺乏背景或者你缺乏权力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last one actually is from Cheryl Sandberg, who I learned an enormous amount from, huge, was like going to business school without going to business school working with her.
zh: 其实最后一条实际上来自 Cheryl Sandberg，我从她那里学到了很多东西，非常多，就像是不用上商学院就在上商学院一样与她共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I say it a lot right now, so I'm going to say it on your podcast so maybe some people will hear me.
zh: 但我现在经常说这句话，所以我会在你的播客上说出来，也许有些人会听到我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Growing more than 100% every year is a bad idea.
zh: 每年增长超过 100% 是一个坏主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: The happiest growth rate is 50%, 100% is manageable.
zh: 最幸福的增长率是 50%，100% 是可控的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything more than doubling and you are signing yourself up for a world of pain.
zh: 任何超过翻倍的增长，你就是在让自己陷入痛苦的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have seen this over and over and over again.
zh: 我一次又一次地看到这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had to scream way louder about it five years ago than I do now because we've been through collectively a lot of pain and a lot of layoffs.
zh: 五年前我必须为此比现在更大声地尖叫，因为我们集体经历了很多痛苦和很多裁员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously the combination of 2021 and then AI has led us to talk about unit economics and scaling with tools, not people.
zh: 显然，2021 年和 AI 的结合导致我们要谈论单位经济学和利用工具而非人来扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I still see companies and I'm still talking to founders that are like, "Yeah, we're 50 people and we're going to be 150 people next year."
zh: 但我仍然看到公司，我仍然在与创始人交谈，他们说，“是的，我们现在 50 人，明年我们要变成 150 人。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, "Could you possibly do that with 100 people?"
zh: 我会说，“你能不能用 100 人来做到这一点？”

speaker: Unknown
en: But here's what basically happens if you grow at more than 100%, which is you're growing too fast to de-dupe all the issues.
zh: 但如果你以超过 100% 的速度增长，基本上会发生的是，你增长得太快，无法对所有问题进行去重。

speaker: Unknown
en: So somebody posts this role, it actually turns out that that role is also being hired for on this other team.
zh: 所以有人发布了这个职位，结果发现那个职位实际上也在这个其他团队招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're hiring two people who more or less have the same job description and are assigned to the same number or the same problem, but nobody talked to each other.
zh: 所以你雇佣了两个人，他们有大致相同的职位描述，并被分配到相同的编号或相同的问题，但没有人互相交谈过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those two people both show up and they're like, "I am doing this."
zh: 然后这两个人都出现了，他们说，“我在做这个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And the person's like, "Wait, I thought I was doing that."
zh: 另一个人说，“等等，我以为我在做那个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, so then you've got all this... And think about all the time and all the energy and all the money that goes into de-duping that.
zh: 无论如何，然后你有了所有这些……想想所有的时间、所有的精力和所有的金钱都花在去重上。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you slow down, if you hire for quality and for real need versus the panic hiring, whatever your sales model spits out or whatever, you'll actually find leverage.
zh: 如果你放慢速度，如果你为了质量和真实需求而招聘，而不是为了恐慌性招聘，无论你的销售模型吐出什么或任何其他东西，你实际上会发现杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: You find, "Oh, I didn't need that person," or, "I didn't need this whole team," or, "I didn't need this whole function," or, "I can wait for that."
zh: 你会发现，“噢，我不需要那个人，”或者，“我不需要这个整个团队，”或者，“我不需要这个整个职能，”或者，“我可以等待那个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So slow down.
zh: 所以放慢速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, these are all just guidelines in terms of the 50% is happy and 100% is manageable.
zh: 同样，这些都只是指导原则，关于 50% 是快乐的，100% 是可控的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But having seen enough of this, I can tell you these are good rules and you should pay attention to them.
zh: 但见识了足够多的这种情况后，我可以告诉你这些都是好的规则，你应该注意它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes you're like, "I have to double or I have to more than double or I have to triple," or whatever.
zh: 有时你会说，“我必须翻倍，或者我必须翻倍以上，或者我必须三倍，”或者其他什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "Okay, just ask a whole lot of questions as you open roles.
zh: 我会说，“好的，只是在开放职位时问很多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ask a whole lot of questions as you hire because you will find duplication, you will find chaos coming in the front door."
zh: 在招聘时问很多问题，因为你会发现重复，你会发现混乱从前门进来了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: More people does not actually make you faster.
zh: 更多的人并不会真的让你更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We think it does.
zh: 我们认为它会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does not.
zh: 它不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it harder.
zh: 它会让事情变得更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it harder to get work done.
zh: 它会让完成工作变得更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes it slower.
zh: 它会让事情变得更慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you should be scared of adding people, not like, "Oh, this is the answer to all my problems."
zh: 所以你应该害怕增加人手，而不是觉得，“噢，这是我所有问题的答案。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

en: And just to be clear, you're talking about the growth of the company.
zh: 为了清楚起见，你是在谈论公司的增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: So doubling in a year, bad idea.
zh: 所以一年内翻倍，是个坏主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's possible, but you're saying it's going to be very hard and painful and probably a really bad idea.
zh: 这是可能的，但你是说这会非常艰难和痛苦，而且可能真的是个坏主意。

speaker: Molly Graham
en: Yeah. More than doubling head count growth.
zh: 是的。超过两倍的人员增长。

zh: 超过两倍。

en: Great point.

en: This is top of mind because I just had the interview with Matt McGinnis, but so much of what he talked about is this resonates with what you're talking about.

en: He talked a lot about under-resourcing your team-
zh: 他谈了很多关于为团队配备资源不足的问题——

speaker: Molly Graham
en: Totally.

en: Leads to much better outcomes because people don't work on the low priority stuff.

en: And the other is this idea of escalating.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like, "Escalation is good.

en: Tell me when there's something I can help with, please.
zh: 请告诉我有什么我可以帮忙的，

speaker: Lenny
en: "To help."

en: Yeah, 100%.

zh: 太棒了。所以也许作为最后一个问题，你的一位前同事，Eric Antonow，他是个极好的人，很少有人知道——

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: That I've chatted with over the last few months because he knows so many people that come on this podcast.

en: He's a former Facebook person, now at OpenAI.
zh: 他是个前 Facebook 员工，现在在 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked him what I should ask you about and he told me something really insightful about you.
zh: 我问他我该问你什么，他告诉我一些关于你的非常有见地的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said that you had this really massive growth spurt at Facebook, which you shared and talked about.
zh: 他说你在 Facebook 有过一次真正的大规模爆发式增长，你分享并谈论了这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after you leaving, you had this huge ambition to become COO, CEO, become this huge big deal boss person, just take over the world.
zh: 在你离开之后，你有这种巨大的雄心想要成为 COO、CEO，成为这种大老板级的人物，接管世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he noticed your ambitions significantly pivot to working on community building and helping people with their careers.
zh: 然后他注意到你的雄心显著转向了社区建设和帮助人们发展职业生涯。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you turned down really big C-level role opportunities.
zh: 而且你拒绝了一些真正巨大的 C 级职位机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way he described it is you were a dog that once thought you were cat.
zh: 他描述的方式是你是一只曾经以为自己是一只猫的狗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other metaphor he used is you change from AC current to DC current, which I don't know exactly what that means.
zh: 他用的另一个比喻是你从交流电变成了直流电，我不确切知道那是什么意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: So does this resonate?
zh: 所以这有共鸣吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if so, just what happened there?
zh: 如果有的话，那里发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Eric is actually better at metaphors than I am, and I regularly rip his metaphors.
zh: Eric 实际上比我更擅长比喻，而且我经常剽窃他的比喻。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yes, Eric Antonow, the least well-known, but most brilliant person in my life.
zh: 是的，Eric Antonow，我生命中知名度最低，但最辉煌的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I gave a talk at a company recently and somebody asked the question, "What's something you've changed your mind about?"
zh: 所以我最近在一家公司做了一个演讲，有人问了一个问题，“有什么事情是你改变了主意的？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, "Woof."
zh: 我当时就像，“哇哦。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But I actually talked about this because... So my brain is developing this model that is not done yet, but it's basically this idea that everybody has a proving phase to their career where you're proving to yourself and probably to your parents and some other people that you're good at stuff.
zh: 但我实际上谈到了这个，因为……所以我的大脑正在开发这个模型，虽然还没完成，但基本上就是这个想法，每个人的职业生涯都有一个验证阶段，你要向自己，可能还有你的父母和其他人证明你擅长某些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, "I'm going to prove."
zh: 你就像，“我要去证明。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's an important phase because you need to learn.
zh: 这是一个重要的阶段，因为你需要学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the stuff we talked about.
zh: 我们谈论过的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to learn what you're good at.
zh: 你需要了解你擅长什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to learn that you are good at things and that people should hire you for things and what are those things?
zh: 你需要了解你擅长事情，并且人们应该因为这些事情雇佣你，以及那些事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: But part of that phase is also doing what you think matters, what you think you should do.
zh: 但那个阶段的一部分也是做你认为重要的事情，做你认为你应该做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Family programming or career books tell you this is what you should do, titles and all that stuff.
zh: 家庭编程或职业书籍告诉你这是你应该做的事情，头衔以及所有那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, I think everybody has a moment and I think this moment varies wildly in terms of when it hits people, where you hit some sort of wall or I don't know what it is, speed bump, something, and the world forces you to say, "Okay, I've proven myself and I'm good at this thing.
zh: 然后，我认为每个人都有一个时刻，我认为这个时刻在什么时候击中人们方面差异很大，你会遇到某种墙或者我不知道它是什么，减速带，某种东西，世界强迫你说，“好的，我已经证明了自己，我擅长这件事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do I want to do with it?"
zh: 我想用它做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, I spent 10 or 15 years proving to myself and to others that I was really good at this thing, basically working with brilliant founders to help bring their vision to life, "That's what you should hire me to do."
zh: 对我来说，我花了 10 年或 15 年的时间向自己和他人证明我真的很擅长这件事情，基本上是与聪明的创始人合作，帮助将他们的愿景变为现实，“这就是你应该雇佣我做的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I was known for.
zh: 这就是我出名的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it turned out that that wasn't what I love doing anymore.
zh: 结果证明，那不再是我喜欢做的事情了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was really, really hard to walk away from because there was a lot of shoulds.
zh: 真的很难从中抽身，因为有很多“应该”。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, "You should take this job with this fancy title.
zh: 就像，“你应该接受这份拥有这个花哨头衔的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: People are going to think you're so cool."
zh: 人们会觉得你很酷。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And you get to... I call it a LinkedIn crush where you're really excited to post the job on LinkedIn, but you're deeply unexcited about doing the job.
zh: 然后你可以……我称之为 LinkedIn Crush，你对在 LinkedIn 上发布这份工作感到非常兴奋，但对做这份工作深感不兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have all these LinkedIn crushes and you're like... And I vividly remember this one job that I turned down where I had to go for many walks.
zh: 所以你有所有这些 LinkedIn Crush，你就像……而且我生动地记得我拒绝的那份工作，我不得不散步了很多次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I was repeating over and over again to myself was, "What does this get you that you don't already have?
zh: 我一遍又一遍地对自己重复的是，“这能给你带来什么你没有的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does this get you that you don't already have?"
zh: 这能给你带来什么你没有的东西？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, for me, it was this realization that these things that fed me early in my career just didn't feed me anymore, that I didn't get joy and excitement out of doing these jobs anymore, and I wasn't scared.
zh: 我认为，对我来说，这种认识是，这些在职业生涯早期滋养我的事情不再滋养我了，我不再从做这些工作中获得快乐和兴奋，而且我不害怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it led me actually on a very long, windy journey, a founder journey, even though I have trouble with that title, just like the influencer title, to figure out what I wanted to build.
zh: 所以这实际上让我踏上了一段非常漫长、曲折的旅程，一段创始人旅程，尽管我对这个头衔有 trouble，就像对网红那个头衔一样，去弄清楚我想要构建什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I would've told you I wanted to build three years ago is actually not what I'm doing today, but through a lot of really fun experiments and a journey that never ends, what I've discovered is that what I love doing is building safe spaces for leaders to learn and grow, but also to find sanity and connection in a world that's kind of insane, whether it's working in a startup or some other kind of insanity, but that feeds me and there's nothing I love more than that, and I could not have told you that three years ago, but, to Eric's point, it really took a lot of work to switch currents or switch myself from a dog to a cat or whatever his metaphor is.
zh: 三年前我会告诉你我想构建的东西实际上不是我今天在做的事情，但通过很多有趣的实验和一段永不结束的旅程，我发现我喜欢做的是为领导者建立安全的空间去学习和成长，但也在一个有点疯狂的世界中找到理智和连接，无论是在初创公司工作还是某种其他类型的疯狂，但这滋养了我，没有什么比这更让我喜欢的了，三年前我无法告诉你这一点，但是，正如 Eric 的观点，这确实需要很多工作来切换水流或将自己从狗变成猫，或者不管他的比喻是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's the work of it's ongoing work, but it's that thing of what do I want versus what do I think people expect of me?
zh: 我认为这是正在进行的工作，但这是我想要的 vs 我认为人们期望我做什么的那回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much depth there.
zh: 那里有太多的深度。

speaker: Unknown
en: This could be another entire podcast conversation talking through this journey, but I'm going to close with a note from your partner, Sarah.
zh: 这可以成为另一整场关于这段旅程的播客对话，但我将以你合作伙伴 Sarah 的留言作为结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: She told me that she has this sticker on her notebook with three pieces of advice that you gave her when she started at OpenAI.
zh: 她告诉我，她的笔记本上有一个贴纸，上面有你在她开始工作时给她的三条建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get to know your customer, they have the answer; be patient because everything is going to change; and just keep trying.
zh: 了解你的客户，他们有答案；要有耐心，因为一切都会改变；并且只是继续尝试。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just as a final question, is there anything along those lines that you think might be helpful for people to hear or is there anything else you want to share or leave listeners with?
zh: 所以作为最后一个问题，你认为有什么类似的事情可能会对人们有帮助吗？或者你还有什么想分享或留给听众的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of what I think is so important to realize inside of scaling and changing companies and the world is some things will always be true.
zh: 我认为在规模化和变革中的公司以及世界内部，意识到这一点如此重要的一部分是，有些事情将永远是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of what I was saying to Sarah in the "get to know the customer, they have the answer" is, whatever bullshit is going on around you and whatever walls and ceiling are being rearranged this week, the customer is never going to change.
zh: 我对 Sarah 说的“了解客户，他们有答案”的一部分是，无论你周围发生了什么 bullshit，无论这周墙壁和天花板如何重新排列，客户永远不会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a thing that will never change.
zh: 那是一件永远不会改变的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think finding those immovable objects, those compasses in the face of a storm, which being inside of a scaling company in a startup feels like a tornado.
zh: 我认为在风暴中找到那些不可移动的物体，那些指南针，身处规模化的公司或初创公司内部感觉就像一场龙卷风。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think OpenAI is extra special on that front.
zh: 我认为 OpenAI 在这方面特别特殊。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to find these guiding lights that get you through that storm.
zh: 你必须找到这些指引之光，带你度过那场风暴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's sort of the same thing as "Serve the business, not the people."
zh: 我认为这与“服务业务，而不是人”是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the things that will always be true?
zh: 有哪些事情将永远是真的？

speaker: Unknown
en: We are here to do this.
zh: 我们在这里是为了做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are here to serve the customer.
zh: 我们在这里是为了服务客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other piece of the three things that she wrote down is, I think that we, as humans, we seek stability.
zh: 她写下的三件事中的另一部分是，我认为我们作为人类，我们寻求稳定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our brains would like things to stop changing.
zh: 我们的大脑希望事情停止变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would like things to stay the same.
zh: 我们希望事情保持原样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is just not a reality inside of companies that are growing and changing as fast as OpenAI or a lot of the companies today that are being built.
zh: 这在像 OpenAI 或今天正在建立的许多公司这样快速成长和变化的公司内部根本不是现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually, you need to start to expect instability.
zh: 所以实际上，你需要开始期待不稳定。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to start to just assume things are going to change.
zh: 你需要开始只是假设事情会改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Assume you're going to have a new boss in six months.
zh: 假设你六个月后会有一个新老板。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk about this a lot when I talk to folks at OpenAI, "You need to stop expecting that anything's going to be the same in six months or a year.
zh: 当我和 OpenAI 的人交谈时，我经常谈论这一点，“你需要停止期待六个月或一年后任何事情会保持不变。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will have a different job.
zh: 你将有一份不同的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will have a different boss."
zh: 你将有一个不同的老板。”

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you prepare for that?
zh: 你如何为此做准备？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you know what I mean?
zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you almost see the instability as stability because it's the only thing that is definitely going to be true.
zh: 你如何几乎把这种不稳定视为稳定，因为它是唯一肯定会成真的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of that is to just keep going.
zh: 其中一部分就是继续前行。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know what I mean?
zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: To just find these lights and these compasses or whatever metaphor sticks with you and focus on those because whatever is happening around you, you just got to keep moving forward and keep learning as much as you can because that's the real opportunity.
zh: 就是去找到这些光和这些指南针，或者任何能引起共鸣的比喻，并专注于它们，因为无论你周围发生什么，你必须继续前进并尽可能多地学习，因为那是真正的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever happens to the company, however successful it is, all that you take away from it... I always say all that you take away from it is people that like working with you and want to work with you again and what you learned.
zh: 无论公司发生了什么，无论它多么成功，你从中带走的一切……我总是说，你从中带走的一切是那些喜欢与你共事并想再次与你共事的人，以及你学到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's it.
zh: 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might hopefully take a bunch of money, but you might not.
zh: 你可能希望能赚很多钱，但也可能赚不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people and what you learned, that's it.
zh: 所以是人和你学到的东西，就这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Focus on that.
zh: 专注于那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all about the friends you made along the way.
zh: 这全在于你在这个过程中结交的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: That old line is true.
zh: 那句老话是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, man.
zh: 噢，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Molly, I feel like we've gone for so long and we've just scratched the surface.
zh: Molly，我觉得我们聊了很久，但我们只是刚刚触及皮毛。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to have you back to go deeper on a lot of this stuff.
zh: 我很希望能请你回来深入探讨其中的很多事情。

en: I'm going to skip the lightning round because we've gone long and I want to keep people from having to listen to more.
zh: 我要跳过闪电战环节，因为我们已经聊得很久了，我想让大家不用再听更多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm just going to end with, what should people know about what you're working on?
zh: 所以我就以此为结尾，人们应该对你正在做的事情了解些什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where can people go find you online?
zh: 人们可以在哪里找到你？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how can listeners be useful to you?
zh: 听众如何能对你有所帮助？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can find me on LinkedIn and you can find me on Substack.
zh: 你可以在 LinkedIn 上找到我，你也可以在 Substack 上找到我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a Substack called Lessons that I'm slowly trying to turn into a community where we can talk about things, the real stuff.
zh: 我有一个叫 Lessons 的 Substack，我正慢慢试图把它变成一个社区，我们可以讨论事情，真实的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can find me at Glue Club, which, if you're a leader inside of one of these crazy companies that's changing all the time, we can be a great home for you.
zh: 你可以在 Glue Club 找到我，如果你是这些不断变化的疯狂公司中的一名领导者，我们可以成为你的绝佳归宿。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the URL there just for folks to check out?
zh: 那里的网址是什么，方便大家去看看吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's glueclub.com.
zh: 是 glueclub.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: Glue, G-L-U-E?
zh: Glue，G-L-U-E？

speaker: Unknown
en: G-L-U-E.
zh: G-L-U-E。

speaker: Unknown
en: C-L-U-B.com.
zh: C-L-U-B.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, exactly.
zh: 是的，没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in terms of people, what people can do to be useful to me, I love helping leaders with problems.
zh: 至于人们方面，人们能做的对我有用的事情，我喜欢帮助领导者解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really get a lot of energy out of unsticking people and helping people feel supported and seen and helping them grow.
zh: 我真的从帮人摆脱困境中获得很多能量，帮助人们感到被支持和被看见，并帮助他们成长。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do that through Glue Club.
zh: 我通过 Glue Club 做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're a leader that feels like you want some sanity and some support in the face of whatever tornado you're in, that's a great place to come.
zh: 所以如果你是一名领导者，觉得在面对你所处的任何风暴时需要一些理智和支持，那是一个很好的去处。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the same is true of Substack.
zh: Substack 也是一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if Glue Club isn't for you, come on over to Substack.
zh: 所以如果 Glue Club 不适合你，就来 Substack 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've opened up a bunch of channels to just talk about stuff, listen to people's problems, answer questions because I love helping people.
zh: 我开辟了很多渠道来讨论事情，倾听人们的问题，回答问题，因为我喜欢帮助人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's a complicated moment right now to be a leader and to figure out which way is up.
zh: 而且我认为现在作为一名领导者并弄清方向是复杂的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So come on over.
zh: 所以快来吧。

en: Amazing.
